page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-3xL4 is a GPU-accelerated virtual server instance configured on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 CPU architecture with 16 shared vCPUs and 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring external block storage volumes for persistent data.

The primary hardware feature of this instance is its graphics acceleration capability, powered by three NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture. These GPUs provide a combined total of 72 GB of VRAM. This configuration is designed for workloads that benefit from parallel processing, such as machine learning inference, video transcoding, and data science pipelines.

From a resource density perspective, the combination of 192.0 GB of system RAM and three dedicated accelerators offers a balanced profile for memory-intensive GPU workloads. Because the 16 vCPUs use a shared allocation model, CPU-bound sequential processing may experience resource contention, making this server most cost-efficient for tasks that offload the primary computational burden to the NVIDIA L4 GPUs rather than relying on sustained, dedicated host CPU performance.
